title: Reload a grease gun: catch the follower rod in the end-cap slot, then push a new grease cartridge into the barrel
instruction: Make the grease gun barrel ready for its head: the follower rod pulled all the way back with its neck caught in the slot of the end cap, holding the spring on its own, and the new grease cartridge inside the barrel, open end first, its end flush with the barrel mouth. Leave both arms clear.
context: Done by: automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023.00, 704,640 US workers) and industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041.00, 439,640; BLS OEWS national estimates), whose O*NET task lists include routine lubrication of vehicles and machines. A grease gun is reloaded many times a day; a lever grease gun maker's service guide (guns for 14 oz cartridges) has the user pull the follower rod fully back, lock the rod in the slot of the cylinder end cap, insert the new cartridge open end first, then refit the head and release the rod. Unlike a caulking-gun ratchet, nothing holds the 14 N spring except the rod's neck seated in the keyhole slot: if it is not caught, the follower snaps back and fills the barrel.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (+x forward, +y left), heights above the table. Ribbed rubber bench mat 56 x 64 cm centred at (27, 0). Grease gun barrel (steel, 5.6 cm outside, 5.2 cm bore, 25.0 cm long) clamped in a fixed rubber bench holder with its axis along y at x = 32, 3.8 cm above the table; open mouth at y = +12.5 (head already unscrewed and lying on the mat), rear end cap at y = -12.8. The cap plate has a keyhole: 1.6 cm hole on the axis and a 0.65 cm slot running 1.65 cm straight down. Inside, a follower disc (4.7 cm) on a compression spring, 58 N/m (14 N when drawn back 24 cm). Follower rod 1.0 cm with a 0.5 cm neck right behind the follower and a 10 cm red T-handle, resting at y = -15.9. The holder continues past the mouth as a V-shaped loading rest (y +13.5 to +33) in line with the bore. Grease cartridge, loose, 0.45 kg: tube 5.0 cm diameter, 24.0 cm long, open end toward -y, lying on a fixed two-block rest at (18.5, 21.5), axis 3.4 cm above the table. Fixed layout every trial.
scoring: Evaluated on the current state every control step, with one remembered failure: once the cartridge has fallen off the bench the run scores 0 to the end, even if it is put back. 0.35: follower drawn back >= 230 mm (T-handle >= 23 cm out from the cap) with the rod neck dropped >= 10 mm into the cap slot and no gripper within 6 cm of the T-handle, so the cap holds it. +0.45, only with the rod caught: cartridge in the bore, open end first, its end within 5 mm of the barrel mouth, axis within 5 degrees and 4 mm of the barrel axis. +0.20: all of that, cartridge centre moving < 2 cm/s, both grippers >= 10 cm from the gun, held 2 s. A part missing scores 0; any other end state scores the sum of the tiers it meets. Totals: 0, 0.35, 0.8, 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the T-handle so the neck leaves the slot and let the spring return the rod, pull the cartridge out and lay it back on its rest.
fidelity: Barrel, keyhole cap, rod and 14 oz cartridge at real size (authored dimensions, README). Spring force at full draw: no published figure (maker's guide gives none); estimated 10-20 N, modelled 14 N (58.3 N/m). Rod neck held by real contact with the slot edges, no code-held latch. Cartridge slides in the bore by contact (1 mm play). Barrel clamped in a bench holder. Grease, seals, tab seal not simulated.
